title: why didn't you say goodbye?
music_prompt:
A slow, quiet, heartbroken lo-fi song for a rainy night, like a memory at three in the morning. Soft duet: a gentle, breathy female voice and a warm, low, tired male voice, singing softly and close to the microphone, as if each is talking to the other from a different city. Soft felt piano, a muted electric guitar with light chorus, warm tape hiss, steady soft rain in the background, a very soft dusty lo-fi beat at 68 BPM, gentle sub bass. Key of F major with bittersweet minor chords. Mostly instrumental with soft wordless humming; only the short lines below are sung. No build-up, no loud chorus, no belting, no sudden changes, no fade-in or fade-out: it starts and ends at the same soft level so it loops seamlessly. Feeling: sad but warm, missing someone without anger.

Lyrics:
[Intro: soft humming, female and male]

[Verse 1, female]
Your cup is still here by the window,
the rain keeps your seat warm tonight.

[Verse 1, male]
I waited for the train you never took,
the station lights kept me company.

[Chorus, both, very soft]
Why didn't you say goodbye?
I'd have held you one more time.

[Instrumental: piano, guitar and rain, soft humming]

[Outro, both, whispered]
One more time... just one more time.
